target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

macOS hatch and WebChat can make a slow first assistant reply look timed out or stuck when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side run budget. The gateway may have accepted the request and kept the assistant run active, but the macOS client did not consistently give every WebChat send path the same first-run-sized window or refresh history after terminal completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short gateway request/ACK deadline from the assistant run budget. `GatewayConnection.chatSend` keeps its request-sized default so unrelated callers such as Talk Mode retain their existing policy, while all three `MacGatewayChatTransport` paths—direct send, selected-agent/routing-contract send, and outbox route-lease replay—explicitly use a 300,000 ms WebChat run budget.

The shared chat view model now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The shared default remains 120 seconds, macOS WebChat opts into five minutes, and the existing `agent.wait` gateway surface triggers a history refresh after a terminal result. The patch does not change gateway protocol shape, provider routing, authentication, model selection, channel delivery, schema, migrations, or session persistence.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant can keep seeing an accepted slow first reply as pending beyond 30 seconds instead of receiving a premature client timeout. Gateway connection failures still use the short request deadline, and a terminal assistant result refreshes history and clears the pending run through the shared chat state owner.

## Evidence

- Exact local head: `e594c6b082df19626b88caeac568a9bde2a09cb5`.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --skip-update --filter GatewayConnectionControlTests` — 23 tests passed. Coverage includes request/run timeout separation, direct and targeted WebChat sends, outbox route-lease replay, `agent.wait` request encoding, and terminal-versus-active completion reconciliation.
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --skip-update --filter "completion wait"` — 3 tests passed. Coverage includes completion-triggered history refresh and pending clear, the shared 120-second default, and the transport-specific 300-second override.
- `corepack pnpm native:i18n:check` — passed with `entries=2869 changed=false`.
- Targeted SwiftFormat for the changed gateway/control test passed. The changed-Swift lint reports six diagnostics in untouched regions of `ChatViewModelTests.swift`; the same six rules reproduce against `origin/main` at the corresponding baseline lines. `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passes.
- A current-head arm64 OpenClaw app bundle built successfully with `swift build --package-path apps/macos -c debug --product OpenClaw --arch arm64 --skip-update`; its ad-hoc signature passed strict codesign verification. The independently resolved Talk Mode MLX TTS helper was omitted after dependency resolution timed out, and WebChat does not invoke that helper.
- Current-head live pending proof exercised `OpenClawChatViewModel` and `MacGatewayChatTransport` against a real local gateway. At 32.05 seconds, the gateway was healthy, the request ACK had returned (`is_sending=false`), the assistant run remained tracked (`pending_run_count=1`), and no client error was present. This proves the production path survives the former 30-second cutoff. The isolated run was intentionally aborted after the observation and cleaned up.
- This environment did not produce a live model completion because its available provider authentication/model routes failed externally. Completion-triggered history refresh and pending clear are therefore demonstrated by the current-head focused Swift tests above, not claimed as live completion proof.
- Visual composer proof was blocked because the macOS login window covered the app window; no screenshot or click-through proof is claimed.
